claims.claim: The Paley graph G_p is d-regular with d=(p−1)/2; adjacent vertices have (p−5)/4 common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have (p−1)/4. Its adjacency spectrum is {d, ((−1+√p)/2)^((p−1)/2), ((−1−√p)/2)^((p−1)/2)}.
claims.evidence: The quadratic-character correlation sum gives degree d and the two common-neighbor counts. Hence A²+A=((p−1)/4)(I+J); on 1⊥ the eigenvalues solve z²+z−(p−1)/4=0. Dimension and trace zero give multiplicity (p−1)/2 for each root. Exact enumeration through p=101 confirmed every entrywise identity.
claims.search_method: Direct quadratic-character derivation, followed by exhaustive integer graph checks for all admissible primes through 101.

claims.claim: Every feasible degree-four moment matrix may be averaged so that its singleton principal block is N=[[1,a1ᵀ],[a1,aI+bA]], where pa is the objective and b is both the moment and diagonal pair-entry of every edge.
claims.evidence: The affine maps x↦sx+t with nonzero-square s form Paley automorphisms transitive on vertices and edges. Averaging their simultaneous index permutations preserves feasibility, PSD, and objective. Union consistency makes the singleton diagonal equal its first-row moment a and makes the edge singleton entry, empty-to-edge entry, and edge-pair diagonal all equal b; nonedges are zero. The checker exactly confirmed the vertex, edge, and nonedge affine orbits.
claims.search_method: Orbit and moment-consistency proof, supplemented by exact affine-orbit enumeration.

claims.claim: SOS_2(G_p)=√p, and hence the elementary hierarchy bound gives SOS_4(G_p)≤√p.
claims.evidence: For an averaged degree-two matrix, PSD on the least eigenspace gives b≤a/q, while the empty/all-ones block gives pa²≤a+db. Thus pa≤1+d/q=√p. Equality is attained by a=1/√p and b=2/(p+√p); its least-eigenspace and all-ones Schur eigenvalues vanish and all remaining eigenvalues are nonnegative. Every degree-four feasible matrix has a degree-two feasible principal submatrix. These identities were also checked exactly in Q(√p).
claims.search_method: Complete spectral SDP upper bound and explicit feasible optimizer, with exact quadratic-field checks.

claims.claim: For every finite graph G, SOS_4(G)≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
claims.evidence: Let y_v=Ẽ[x_v] and R_v=Σ_iẼ[x_vx_i]. For y_v>0, f↦Ẽ[x_vf]/y_v is degree-two feasible on the closed neighborhood because Ẽ[x_vq²]=Ẽ[(x_vq)²]≥0; hence R_v≤y_v(1+SOS_2(G[N(v)])). If y_v=0, PSD makes the singleton-v row zero, so R_v=0. With t=Σ_vy_v, PSD on the empty and summed-singleton directions gives t²≤Σ_vR_v, and summing the preceding bounds yields t≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
claims.search_method: Direct pseudoexpectation conditioning and PSD argument; no finite computation is needed.

claims.claim: For nonzero f:F_p→C, |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≥p+1; equivalently, every square minor of the p×p Fourier matrix is nonzero.
claims.evidence: For a Fourier minor, division of its generalized Vandermonde determinant by the ordinary Vandermonde gives an algebraic integer whose reduction modulo 1−ζ is ∏_{i<j}(y_j−y_i)/(j−i), nonzero in F_p. Thus every minor is nonzero. If the two support sizes summed to at most p, selecting as many zero coordinates of f as there are nonzero Fourier coefficients would produce an invertible square minor annihilating that coefficient vector. Conversely, a singular minor constructs such a support-violating vector, proving equivalence. Exact cyclotomic enumeration found all 251 minors for p=5 and all 3431 for p=7 nonzero.
claims.search_method: Prime cyclotomic generalized-Vandermonde proof plus exhaustive exact cyclotomic minor checks for p=5,7.

claims.claim: Let P_- project onto the least-eigenvalue Paley eigenspace and let S_e consist of an edge e and all its common neighbors. With R=|S_e|=(p+3)/4, every real f supported on S_e and equal to 1 at both endpoints satisfies ||P_-f||²≥η₀:=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)).
claims.evidence: If P_-f=0, then f̂ is supported on at most (p+1)/2 frequencies, while f is supported on at most R; their sum is (3p+5)/4<p+1, contradicting claim 4. Thus K=P_-[S_e,S_e] is positive definite. Cauchy–Binet gives det K≥p^(−R)|D|² for a nonzero R×R Fourier minor D. Its nonzero integral field norm and Hadamard bounds on its other p−2 conjugates give |D|²≥R^(−R(p−2)). Since K is a compression of a projection, its eigenvalues are at most one, so λ_min(K)≥det K; the two fixed endpoint values give ||f||²≥2. Selected minors and their nonzero exact norms were checked for p=5,13.
claims.search_method: Fourier-support argument, Cauchy–Binet, cyclotomic norm bound, and exact selected-minor norm checks.

claims.claim: For every prime p≡1 (mod 4), SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, with d=(p−1)/2 and q=(√p+1)/2.
claims.evidence: For an averaged feasible matrix, b is a pair-index diagonal and hence b≥0. For b>0, compressing the singleton/pair-e block to the least eigenspace yields ||P_-c||²≤b(a−qb). Since c/b is supported on S_e and equals one at both endpoints, claim 5 gives ||P_-c||²≥b²η₀, hence b≤a/(q+η₀). Combining this with pa²≤a+db gives pa≤1+d/(q+η₀); b=0 gives pa≤1. Finally 1+d/q=√p and η₀>0, proving strictness. The algebraic identities and strict comparisons were checked without floating point.
claims.search_method: PSD compression and projection-gap proof, supplemented by exact Q(√p) and rational arithmetic checks.

claims.claim: If G is triangle-free and has an edge, then SOS_4(G)=2; in particular SOS_4(G_5)=2.
claims.evidence: For distinct edges e,f in a triangle-free graph, e∪f is not a clique, so the edge-edge block is diagonal with entries z_e≥0. PSD of the empty/edge block gives S=Σ_ez_e≤1. If t is the objective, PSD on the empty and summed-singleton directions gives t²≤t+2S≤t+2, hence t≤2. A genuine edge supplies a rank-one clique-assignment moment matrix of objective two. G_5 has common-neighbor parameter zero and has edges. The checker constructed its exact rank-one matrix and verified the relevant structure for all 434 nonempty triangle-free labeled graphs through five vertices.
claims.search_method: General PSD block proof, exact G_5 witness construction, and exhaustive small-graph structural checks.

target_evidence: The exact target requires fixed ε>0, C>0, and p0 giving SOS_4(G_p)≤Cp^(1/2−ε) for every sufficiently large admissible prime, or a rigorous proof that this quantified assertion is false. The draft proves only SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, where η₀=exp(−Θ(p² log p)); this upper bound divided by √p tends to one, whereas a fixed-power improvement divided by √p would tend to zero. Thus it proves neither side of the requested dichotomy. The universal strict pointwise improvement and supporting structural results are correct and material partial progress, and the final writeup expressly disclaims full resolution. Accordingly target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
